name: 2019 Panel baseline: Munitions Industry Department overseas IT-worker revenue and local-front model

attribution.legal_posture: UN Panel reporting; some claims reproduce Member State information and remain outside criminal adjudication.

caveats: Monthly earnings and remittance language are historical estimates; a universal current pay rule requires newer evidence.
The underlying operational claims are attributed by the Panel to one Member State.

statements: A Member State reported that the designated Munitions Industry Department used subordinate trading corporations to station software programmers and developers abroad for foreign-currency earnings.
Hundreds were reported across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East, earning on average $3,000-$5,000 monthly and remitting a significant portion to controlling DPRK entities.

The reported cover model used a local citizen as nominal company head while DPRK developers actually ran the company and paid for the cover; workers also used foreign websites for disguised freelance work.
The Panel also reported that some workers performed illicit asset theft, including cryptocurrency, in support of DPRK cyber actors.

sources.support: Supports the MID subordination, geography, earnings range, nominal-local-head cover model, disguised freelance work and illicit-asset-theft linkage
